claim: Apple's tariff refunds arose from retroactive reductions in the tariff rate applied under the IEEPA (transcribed 'IPEA') emergency-powers tariff regime and a reduced global tariff rate under Section 122, meaning Apple overpaid tariffs at a higher prior rate on already-imported goods and is now claiming refunds via 'established processes.'
stance_target: The underlying margin trend excludes a one-off refund credit tied to a specific, lapsing rate-change event, not a durable cost improvement
scope_conditions: Apple fiscal Q2 2026 (March quarter), disclosed April 30, 2026
quoted_support: there was the full-quarter benefit from a reduction in the IPEA tariff rates as well as the reduced global tariff rate under Section 122. In terms of applying for a refund of tariffs paid, we are following the established processes, and we plan to reinvest any amount we receive back into US innovation and advanced manufacturing.

claim: Apple's memory-cost impact escalated through FY2026: minimal in the December quarter, higher in March (partly offset by carry-in inventory), and guided 'significantly' higher for June, with management stating costs would keep rising 'beyond the June quarter.'
stance_target: Memory/DRAM cost inflation is a persistent, worsening structural margin headwind independent of tariff effects
quoted_support: In the December quarter, we really had a minimal impact due to memory... For the June quarter... we expect significantly higher memory costs. They are also partly offset by the benefit of carry-in inventory. And while we do not give color beyond June, I can tell you that beyond the June quarter, we believe memory costs will drive an increasing impact on our business.
numbers: 200bps sequential products GM decline in Q2

claim: Apple confirmed a two-pronged AI foundational-model strategy combining a Google collaboration with in-house model development, with Cook stating the Google collaboration 'is going well.'
stance_target: Nature and durability of Apple's AI infrastructure partnerships (Gemini-powering-Siri thesis)
quoted_support: last quarter you talked about Apple foundational models and a two-pronged strategy: the collaboration with Google as well as continuing to work on your own models... [Cook:] The collaboration with Google is going well. We are happy with where things are, and we are happy with the work we are doing independently as well.

claim: Apple's Greater China revenue grew 33% in H1 FY2026 and 28% year-over-year in the March quarter, a quarterly revenue record, with iPhone, Mac mini, and MacBook Air each the top-selling model in their category in urban China.
stance_target: Thesis that China demand for Apple is structurally weak or declining
scope_conditions: Greater China, H1 and Q2 FY2026
quoted_support: We are thrilled with the performance in Greater China. The first half of the year grew 33%. In March, revenue was up 28%—a quarterly revenue record for us... iPhone was the top-selling model in urban China. The Mac mini was the top-selling desktop in China, and the MacBook Air was the top-selling laptop model.

claim: Apple dropped its formal 'net cash neutral' balance-sheet target in Q2 FY2026, opting to evaluate cash and debt independently, while authorizing a new $100 billion buyback and raising the dividend 4% to $0.27/share.
stance_target: Apple's capital-return capacity and balance-sheet flexibility
quoted_support: Net cash neutral has been a valuable framework for our capital structure, and since 2018, we have significantly right-sized our balance sheet and reduced net cash by over $100 billion. As we move ahead, we are no longer providing net cash neutral as a formal target, and we will independently evaluate cash and debt.

claim: Apple's India business is growing strongly (over half of buyers new-to-product across most categories) but Cook describes Apple's share of the world's second-largest smartphone and third-largest PC market as still 'modest.'
stance_target: Scale of Apple's India opportunity relative to its manufacturing diversification there
quoted_support: It is the second-largest smartphone market in the world and the third-largest PC market. Despite doing extremely well there for quite some time, we still have a modest share, which speaks to the opportunity we have.
